### Summary

Each condensation reaction of the thermodynamics options consumes gases and produces at least one condensate, for
example water vapour into liquid water, or ammonia and hydrogen sulfide into solid ammonium hydrosulfide; a reaction
may also produce gases. At equilibrium, a reaction whose condensate is present has its gas partial pressures on the
saturation curve. A reaction whose condensate is absent may sit below that curve, but never above it. kintera writes
this per reaction with a product of gas partial pressures, so one rule covers a single vapour and a reaction of two
vapours alike. The condition is the one used for moist adiabats with several condensing species.[^ch04-conditions-lio18]

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The conditions every saturation-adjustment solve aims for (@eq-ch04-conditions-saturation).

**Data.** Gas mole fractions or concentrations, condensate amounts, $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa]; one constant per reaction.

**Placement.** Inside both solvers of this chapter.

**Activation.** For every reaction listed with `type: nucleation`; other condensates are not adjusted.

**Guarantee / limits.** Met to `ftol` in the logarithm only when the solve converges within `max-iter`.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $p$, $T$, $x_n$, $x_{\mathrm g}$, $N_{\mathrm g}$, $c_n$, $K_r$,
$\nu_{nr}$, $\Delta_r$; reaction
$r$ and species $n$, gases $n < N_{\mathrm g}$ first. Local symbols: $\hat\nu_{nr} = -\nu_{nr}$, the stoichiometric
coefficient of species $n$ in reaction $r$ with the sign turned, so positive for a species the reaction consumes and
negative for one it produces [-]; $p_n = p\,x_n/x_{\mathrm g}$ the partial pressure of gas $n$ [Pa]; $m_r$ the
condensate that reaction $r$ produces, so $c_{m_r}$ is its concentration [mol m$^{-3}$]. The saturation deficit
$\Delta_r$ is defined below. $K_r(T)$ has units Pa$^{\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}}$.

### Derivation

The saturation constant of a reaction is the product of the partial pressures of its gases on the saturation curve,
each raised to its coefficient: gases consumed with a positive power, gases produced with a negative one. Condensed
phases are pure and have unit activity, so they do not appear in the product. For water vapour condensing the constant
is the saturation vapour pressure; for ammonium hydrosulfide it is the product of the ammonia and hydrogen sulfide
partial pressures, with pressure exponent 2. Define the saturation deficit of reaction $r$ as
$\Delta_r = \ln K_r(T) - \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln p_n$, positive when the gases are subsaturated. The
equilibrium conditions are three complementarity relations, for every reaction $r$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
c_{m_r} &\ge 0, \\
\Delta_r &\ge 0, \\
c_{m_r}\,\Delta_r &= 0 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-conditions-saturation}

In words: the condensate amount is never negative, the gases are never supersaturated, and a reaction whose
condensate is present sits exactly on its saturation curve.

The code tests these conditions in logarithms and in mole fractions. Taking the logarithm of the gas product and
substituting $p_n = p\,x_n/x_{\mathrm{g}}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln p_n &= \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln\frac{x_n}{x_{\mathrm{g}}}
  + \Big(\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\Big) \ln p \\
\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln\frac{x_n}{x_{\mathrm{g}}} &= \ln K_r(T) - \Big(\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\Big) \ln p .
\end{aligned}
$$

Both sums run over gases only: `equilibrate_tp` accumulates the pressure exponent in `stoich_sum` over the first
`ngas` species, and the left side, `log_frac_sum`, over gases, keeping condensates out of it
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}). Summed over all species instead, the ammonium hydrosulfide
reaction would get pressure exponent 1, an error of $\ln p$ in its condition. The right side is `logsvp[j]`. Equality
is accepted when the two differ by at most the tolerance `logsvp_eps`, which the callers set from the option `ftol`.
The fixed-energy solver uses the same constant in concentration units, @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv.

### Numerical method

No iteration here: this scheme defines the target. A reaction is out of equilibrium, and joins the active set of the
solvers, when either

1. its left side exceeds $\ln K_r + \epsilon$, so the gases are supersaturated and vapour must condense; or
2. its left side is below $\ln K_r - \epsilon$ while its condensate is present, so condensate must evaporate.

Here $\ln K_r$ stands for the right side of the second line above and $\epsilon$ for the tolerance `logsvp_eps`. A
reaction whose condensate is absent and whose gases are subsaturated stays out of the active set: the inequality in
@eq-ch04-conditions-saturation holds. Both tests are in `equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}).

**Which reactions and condensates take part.** The reactions are those of `type: nucleation`; every other reaction
type is skipped when the equilibrium stoichiometry is read (`NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). So the complementarity holds per nucleation
reaction, not for every condensate in the cell. A condensate that no nucleation reaction produces is never moved by
saturation adjustment. The kintera test input `tests/jupiter.yaml` shows this: it turns liquid water into a
precipitating copy `H2O(l,p)` by a `coagulation` reaction and evaporates that copy by an `evaporation` reaction.
`H2O(l,p)` appears in no nucleation reaction, so a cell holding it in subsaturated air keeps it after the
solve.[^ch04-conditions-precip] Only the kinetic evaporation of @sec-ch06 removes it.

**A gas that is absent.** When a gas of reaction $r$ has zero mole fraction, its logarithm is undefined. Let
$\mathcal A_r$ be the gases of the reaction that are absent, $\nu_{\mathcal A} = \sum_{n\in\mathcal A_r} \hat\nu_{nr}$,
and $\ln \tilde K_r = \ln K_r(T) - (\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}) \ln p$ the right side above. The code puts
each absent gas at the amount $x_n = |\hat\nu_{nr}|\,\rho_r$ that a reaction extent $\rho_r$ would create, and
chooses $\rho_r$ so that the condition holds there:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ln \rho_r &= \frac{1}{\nu_{\mathcal A}} \Big[ \ln \tilde K_r
  - \sum_{n\notin\mathcal A_r,\, n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln\frac{x_n}{x_{\mathrm g}}
  - \sum_{n\in\mathcal A_r} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln\frac{|\hat\nu_{nr}|}{x_{\mathrm g}} \Big] ,
  \qquad |\ln\rho_r| \le \tfrac12 \ln x_{\max} , \\
\Lambda_r &\leftarrow \ln \tilde K_r - \nu_{\mathcal A} , \qquad
\mathsf W_{rn} \leftarrow \frac{\hat\nu_{nr}}{|\hat\nu_{nr}|\,\rho_r} \quad (n \in \mathcal A_r) ,
\end{aligned}
$$

with $x_{\max}$ the largest representable number of the precision, so that the weight $1/\rho_r$ stays finite. The
left side $\Lambda_r$ of the condition (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp) is replaced as shown, so the deficit that the step
removes is $\nu_{\mathcal A}$, and the weight of an absent gas is $\hat\nu_{nr}/x_n$ evaluated at its boundary
amount. A reaction that lacks both a gas it consumes and a gas it produces cannot move in either direction and is
skipped for that iteration (`equilibrate_tp`, {{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}). The
fixed-energy solver does the same in concentrations, without $x_{\mathrm g}$ (`equilibrate_uv`,
{{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}).

|---|---|---|---|
| `test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` | no reaction supersaturated, no cloud in subsaturated air, no negative amount; N and S conserved | RH within $10^{-5}$ of 1; `rtol=1e-12` for N, S | not stated in the test |
| `test_saturation_degenerate_bound.py` | five fixed-energy cells with ammonia vapour absent and both ammonia reactions active converge, and meet the conditions at the returned temperature | diagnostic $\ge 0$; $\ln S < 10^{-4}$, and $> -10^{-4}$ where condensate is present | not stated in the test |
| `test_reaction_equilibrium.py` (`test_missing_gas_on_both_sides_is_blocked`) | a reaction missing a gas on both sides leaves the state unchanged and reports success, at fixed $T$, $p$ and at fixed $U$, $V$ | exact; `rtol=1e-14` | bitwise for TP; round-off of the $Y \leftrightarrow V$ conversion for UV |

: Tests of the equilibrium conditions. {#tbl-ch04-conditions-tests}

`test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` uses two condensates that share a vapour, ammonia ice and ammonium
hydrosulfide, so the pressure exponent 2 of the second reaction is exercised. It also requires that no cell is left
unadjusted with a non-negative diagnostic, and that at most 10 of 2000 random cells fail.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **Ideal gas only.** The fixed-temperature tests use $p_n = p\,x_n/x_{\mathrm{g}}$, and the fixed-energy and partition
  methods use the ideal-gas form $\ln(\mathcal R T)$. The compressibility terms of a non-ideal equation of state are
  not used in these tests, so saturation is checked as if the gas were ideal.
- **Only nucleation reactions are adjusted**, as above.
- **The tolerance holds only after convergence.** With the default `max-iter` of 10, cold starts far from
  equilibrium fail and leave residuals far above `ftol` (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp, Limits).
:::

- Condensates are pure phases with unit activity. Solutions of condensates are not modelled.
